content: The law of identity in logic asserts that an object is identical to itself, symbolically represented as A ≡ A. This principle is upheld in any reflexive relation, and when discussing equality, the statement A is A is considered a tautology. In philosophy, the law of identity is often mistakenly attributed to Aristotle. However, Aristotle did not explicitly formulate it in this way. Wilhelm Wundt credits Gottfried Leibniz with the symbolic formulation A is A. In 2002, Jonathon Keats initiated a petition to establish A = A as statutory law in Berkeley, California. The proposed law explicitly stated that every entity shall be identical to itself. According to the proposal, any entity found to be non-identical to itself would be subject to a fine of up to one-tenth of a cent. Despite the effort, the law did not pass. Nevertheless, this initiative inspired a similar petition drive in Santa Cruz, California.
